Whether we can predict volcanic eruptions is a matter of genuinely conflicting scientific opinion. Some experts argue that prediction is feasible: [d7] states that "volcano prediction is feasible and is common if volcanoes are instrumented," and [d3] notes that scientists are "growing more and more confident at predicting when volcanoes will erupt in the short-term," particularly in the hours before an event. [d4] similarly reports that volcanologists "feel confident that these ever-improving technologies will enable them to predict when an eruption is about to occur," and [d5] highlights that Mt. Etna's eruptions are currently predicted with a 97% success rate.

However, other sources present a more pessimistic view. [d11] (Scientific American) states plainly that "they cannot yet predict a volcanic eruption," and [d12] (Popular Science) says that "predicting exactly when an individual volcano will erupt—and exactly how large that eruption will be—is still impossible." [d13] (The Guardian) adds that "a tool to definitively predict if a volcano is going to erupt does not exist," calling it "the holy grail of volcanology." [d2] questions why, despite unprecedented monitoring tools, scientists "still cannot accurately predict volcanic eruptions," noting that some volcanoes erupt violently without warning while others show signs beforehand.

The data further illustrates the gap: [d6] and [d5] both report that the global forecasting success rate across all volcanoes is only about 20%, and [d8] describes a real-world case where an increased alert level at Whakaari/White Island still failed to anticipate a deadly eruption, underscoring "the unpredictable nature of these complex systems." [d1] (USGS) reinforces this, noting that "volcanoes do not work in predictable ways and their eruptions do not follow predictable schedules." In summary, while short-term forecasting is improving and some well-monitored volcanoes can be predicted with high accuracy [d5], the scientific community has not reached consensus, and definitive, reliable prediction for most volcanoes worldwide remains an unsolved challenge [d11][d12][d13].
